newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, swap rates stabilised.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, swap rates stabilised.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late Thursday trading, dealers said.
They said short-dated swap rates had eased after soaring in early trade on fears of possible tight supply on Friday.
One local bank dealer said offshore operators who went long on dollars previously were squeezed by local players.
"I think many offshore operators were forced to cut losses following the expensive roll-over costs," he said.
He said, however, the rise in swap premiums caused local interest rates to rise which also induced ample rupiah supply in the afternoon and in turn helping tom/next swaps to ease.
Tom/next swap was last at 1.9/2.3 after hitting a high of 2.8 points in the morning. Overnight swap was at 0.65/0.80.
Overnight money fell to 12.0 percent from 15.0/16.0.
Dealers said declines in short-term money rates indicated that liquidity might not be as tight as feared earlier.
Operators were initially worried over a possible repeat of tight rupiah supply in the money market ahead of the weekend as had happened in the past three Fridays.
Spot rupiah was last at 2,324.0/24.5 at 0905 GMT against an opening of 2,324.5/25.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,321.5/22.25 and 2,320.25/20.75, respectively.
Dealers said swap premiums edged up slightly, driven by early rises in short-dated swap rates. But they said buyers seemed to hold back for now.
One-month swap edged up to 18.0/19.0 from 17.8/18.2, two to 36.0/38.0 from 34.5/36.5, three to 52.0/54.0 from 51.5/52.5 and six to 102.0/102.5 from 101.0/102.5 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,317/2,509 and the conversion rate at 2,317/2,365 on Wednesday.
